Bug_Details:
A field was set twice in the same chained expression. Proto and AutoValue builders provide a fluent interface for constructing
instances. Unlike argument lists, however, they do not prevent the user from
providing multiple values for the same field. Setting the same field multiple times in the same chained expression is
pointless (as the intermediate value will be overwritten), and can easily mask a
bug, especially if the setter is called with different arguments. return MyProto.newBuilder()
    .setFoo(copy.getFoo())
    .setFoo(copy.getBar())
    .build(); return MyProto.newBuilder()
    .setFoo(copy.getFoo())
    .setFoo(copy.getBar())
    .build();
Bug_Explanation: The field 'foo' is set twice in the same chained expression within the builder pattern; the second call overwrites the value set by the first call, which is redundant and can lead to unintended behavior.
Trigger_Explanation: In the testShowBug method, the instance of MyProto is created by calling the showBug method on RedundantSetterCallExample. The showBug method sets the 'foo' property twice consecutively, with the second call overwriting the first. The test asserts the 'foo' to be 'firstValue', but due to the bug, it becomes 'secondValue'.
